bio_draft: Antariksh Daddy is the DJ and producer name of Anandit Sachdev, a record collector and researcher based in Delhi. He started DJing in Berlin in 2015 and, after returning to India in 2018, founded Antariksh Records, a label and community project for dance music in South Asia. He has played in Germany, Egypt and Indonesia, and released the breakbeat EP Stank Face Star Sign on Antariksh Records in 2023.
notes: Homegrown (2023) links a second Instagram, https://www.instagram.com/ananditsachdev/ (personal account); Nomads links @antarikshdaddy, used above. Bandcamp page antarikshdaddy.bandcamp.com was linked by Magnetic Fields but the fetch permission timed out, so releases there were not read and no bandcamp_id is given. Wild City (2022) names Anandit Sachdev as AarAv, label head of Antariksh Records; the Wild City #209 label mix does not name who mixed it, so it is not listed. Spotify embed for a track exists (open.spotify.com/track/48lw8uCWnQLd0K6mD70P0f) but no artist URL was confirmed. No boxout.fm page found for him in this pass.

bio_draft: brnsctr is the producer name of Abhinav Singh, an Indian producer of experimental electronic music, named by Wild City in 2014 among Bangalore's bedroom producers. In 2016 he released the surprise ten-track album ARTLESS, and he presented the show Third Block on New Delhi's boxout.fm.
notes: Identity is a judgement call: the boxout show host and the Wild City producer share the handle brnsctr, but no single page joins them. Param should confirm before publishing the bio. based_city Bengaluru comes from a 2014 Wild City piece and may be out of date; no current city found. Our record genre 'soul' matches the boxout show blurb only. The Third Block Mixcloud link is boxout.fm's show playlist, not a single mix. Bandcamp brnsctr.bandcamp.com is linked from the 2016 Wild City article but was not opened (Bandcamp fetch permission timed out earlier), so no bandcamp_id.

bio_draft: Corridors is the solo electronic project of Delhi musician Rijul Victor, who also drums for the Delhi metal band Colossal Figures. He debuted in 2016 with the single April Flows featuring Nisa Shetty, and his 2020 EP g/old moved into moody trip-hop and jazz-inspired rhythms.

notes: Many artists worldwide are called Corridors; only Delhi/Rijul Victor pages were used. Rolling Stone India says a debut album 'Modree' was due October 13 but shows no year, so it is not listed as a release. The g/old bandcamp_id comes from the album= value in Wild City's embedded Bandcamp player; the Bandcamp page itself was not opened. A YouTube upload of April Flows (A_H6TuLNSmg) is on a third-party 'Ambient' channel, so it was not used.

bio_draft: D80 is the DJ and live act of Anubhav Sharma, who grew up in Delhi, spent time in Los Angeles and returned to Delhi to play disco. His DJ sets cover disco from different eras and places, his live sets use synthesisers and analogue gear, and he hosts the show Across The Universe on boxout.fm.
notes: Many artists use the name D80; only boxout.fm, Wild City and Magnetic Fields pages tied to Anubhav Sharma were used. Wild City also links Facebook facebook.com/D80musiq. He played Boxout Weekender 2019 (6 April, Auro Kitchen & Bar) and was on REProduce's Le Guess Who? COSMOS lineup on 15 May 2022 (Wild City news 19655). The Mixcloud link is boxout.fm's show playlist, not a single mix. No releases found.

bio_draft: Daisho is the electronic music alias of designer Angad Bharaj, from Pune and now based in Bangalore. He hosted The ATYP Hour on boxout.fm and played Boxout Weekender 2018 with a set of funk, disco, world and house. His debut single Simba came out on On the Corner Records.
notes: Simba year 2016 comes from the SoundCloud profile text, which links a Stamp the Wax premiere dated 2016/04/21 in its URL; the premiere page itself was not opened. Refuge Worldwide names his latest album as In Hiding but gives no year, so it is not listed. Wild City says 'from Pune', Refuge (2024) says 'stationed in Bangalore'. The Mixcloud account atypmusic is the one boxout.fm embedded for his Weekender set; it appears to be the ATYP account rather than a personal one. Wild City also lists him opening BoxoutWednesdays #050 for Eclair Fifi (undated). Facebook: facebook.com/daishomusic (Wild City). fbi.radio piece on boxout.fm acts (https://www.fbi.radio/?p=74818) was blocked (permission timed out).

bio_draft: Dakta Dub is a Hyderabad selector and radio presenter who began DJing in 2004 in Budapest, where he hosted the show Indian Lights on Tilos Radio. Back in Hyderabad from 2008, he started Monkey Radio and the bass night Bass Sanskriti, and he hosted Dub Rituals on boxout.fm, a show of meditative dub, chillout and psychedelic ambient.
notes: Not Delhi-based: every source puts him in Hyderabad. Homegrown gives his name as Swayampakula Balasubramaniam (legal name, not stored as an alias). The website field is Monkey Radio, the station he co-founded, not a personal site. Goa Sunsplash's page slug pairs him with 'Monkey Sound System', but the page text does not describe it, so it is not listed as an alias. No releases found.

bio_draft: Delhi Sultanate is the stage name of Taru Dalmia, a reggae and dancehall artist from New Delhi. He is the MC and a founding member of BASSFoundation, lead singer of The Ska Vengers, and runs BFR Sound System with Begum X. On boxout.fm he hosted Dubplates And 45s, a vinyl-only show of dub and reggae.
notes: Kind is a judgement: on boxout.fm he is a vinyl selector, but he is also an MC and singer (The Ska Vengers). Related acts not stored as aliases because they have other members: The Ska Vengers (band), BASSFoundation (group), BFR Sound System (with Begum X aka Samara Chopra), Word Sound Power (with Chris McGuinness). Wild City also links Facebook facebook.com/delhisultanatemusic. Wild City's bio says he grew up partly in Germany and the Bay Area. The Rock Street Journal (rsjonline) article shows no year. Our record has city null; sources say Delhi.
